title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing — v21
author: Priya Patel
summary: High-level product overview and PRD for Unified Inference v21: clarifies the scope of work for the next two quarters, success metrics, design constraints, pricing/packaging updates, and release notes for the GA ship. This document is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders.
product_overview: Objective: Deliver a single unified inference offering that makes it easy for customers to choose a deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private) with consistent API semantics, improved cost controls, and a simpler pricing model. Key capabilities in v21: 1) Model routing by cost/latency policy, 2) Per-customer quantization profile presets, 3) New SKU-based pricing with reserved and burst tiers, 4) Console improvements for rollouts and cost diagnostics.
goals_and_success_metrics:
Primary goals:
- Reduce average per-token cost by 12% for customers using Optimize recommendations (target metric: cost-per-token; baseline measured Q3 2027).
- Achieve 99.95% availability for Hosted API in primary regions (SLO).
- Decrease mean time to rollback after a bad model rollout to < 10 minutes for Dedicated customers.
Success metrics (OKRs):
1) Product adoption: 25% of active customers (by revenue) enable unified routing within 3 months of GA.
2) Performance: median 99th-percentile p99 latency for text-generation under 512 tokens <= 230ms for Hosted API.
3) Revenue: 15% uplift in Dedicated Reserved capacity contracts quarter-over-quarter driven by simplified SKUs.
requirements:
User-facing requirements:
1. Single unified API remains backward compatible with existing /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints.
2. New route-level cost controls: max_cost_per_request and preferred_model_tier.
3. Console: a cost-simulator that shows estimated monthly spend given historical traffic (CSV import).
4. Quantization profiles: customers can choose from 'performance', 'balanced', 'compact' presets.
System requirements (table):
| Requirement ID | Title | Priority | Owner | Acceptance Criteria |
| RQ-001 | Backwards-compatible API | Must | API Platform | No breaking changes to /v1 endpoints; integration tests pass. |
| RQ-002 | Route-level cost control | High | Runtime | API supports max_cost_per_request; docs and SDKs updated. |
| RQ-003 | Multi-tier SKU pricing | High | Pricing & Billing | Billing emits sku_id and line_item with reserved/burst tags. |
| RQ-004 | Quantization preset manager | Medium | Serving Runtime | Presets apply at allocation time; telemetry reports accuracy delta <= 3% vs baseline. |
Operational non-functional requirements:
- Telemetry: emit cost_breakdown, model_variant, quant_profile for each request.
- Security: all changes comply with our current KMS/HSM usage and RBAC model.
- Scalability: system must support 2x current peak traffic with 5-minute autoscale reaction time.
Examples and CLI snippets:
- Example API call to set route-level controls:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/my-route/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"preferred_model_tier":"balanced","max_cost_per_request":0.12}'
```
- Billing example line item (JSON for reference):
```
{ "sku_id": "ui-reserved-64", "quantity": 1, "tags": ["reserved","us-west-2"], "unit_price": "1500.00" }
```
design_specs:
High-level design:
- Control plane: extend routing engine with policy weights and fallback chains. Persist route policy configs in config-service (Postgres schema change: routes.policy jsonb).
- Serving runtime: add quantization-profile lookup during model allocation; default to 'balanced' if unset.
- Billing pipeline: tag requests at the edge with sku_hint and aggregate into daily usage batches.
Key tables/fields (DDL examples):
```
ALTER TABLE routes ADD COLUMN policy jsonb DEFAULT '{}';
CREATE TABLE quant_profiles (id text PRIMARY KEY, description text, preset jsonb);
```
Component interactions:
1) API request hits edge -> edge tags request with route_id -> route policy evaluated in control plane -> request forwarded to serving cluster with model_variant and quant_profile headers -> runtime serves tokens and emits telemetry to ingestion pipeline.
Performance constraints and benchmarks:
- Target p95 token throughput per GPU: 1,200 tokens/sec for seq_len<=512 (measured on A100-80GBequiv).
- KV-cache hit-rate target: >= 65% for conversational workloads with prefix caching enabled.
Compatibility and fallbacks:
- If preferred_model_tier is unavailable, runtime must fall back to next-compatible tier and emit fallback_reason metric.
Security considerations:
- Quantization profiles are treated as config and stored encrypted at rest. Only users with route:edit permission can change presets.
Open design decisions (ADRs to follow):
- ADR-XX: default quantization preset selection algorithm (static vs workload-profiled).
- ADR-YY: SKU bundling strategy for small-volume customers.
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap (next 6 months):
- Month 0-1 (Stabilize): API compatibility layer, config-service schema, unit/e2e tests.
- Month 2-3 (Pilot): Enable quantization presets and route-level cost controls for alpha customers; onboard 3 pilot customers (internal list).
- Month 4 (GA readiness): Console cost-simulator, billing pipeline changes, performance tuning and SRE runbook updates.
- Month 5-6 (GA and Scale): Gradual public rollout, sales enablement, customer success playbooks.
Cross-cutting themes:
- Observability-first: every feature must include telemetry and dashboards before release.
- Cost-conscious UX: prioritize making tradeoffs visible to customers (simulator, recommended presets).
- Backwards-compatibility: minimize migration friction and provide automated migration scripts where possible.
Milestones and owner list:
- API & SDK updates (Owner: API Platform, Target: M1 end)
- Runtime quantization (Owner: Serving Runtime, Target: M2 end)
- Billing SKU rollout (Owner: Finance & Billing, Target: M3)
- Console + cost-simulator (Owner: DX Console, Target: M3)
- Pilot rollout and feedback loop (Owner: Customer Success, Target: M3)
Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Model quality regression after aggressive quantization -> Mitigation: automatic rollback + accuracy guardrails and per-route thresholds.
- Risk: Billing mismatch during SKU transition -> Mitigation: parallel billing mode and reconciliation job for first 30 days.
pricing_and_packaging:
New simplified pricing model (effective GA date):
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go token pricing with an optional Reserved Capacity SKU.
  - Base token rate: $0.0006/token (text-gen), Embedding: $0.0004/vector (128-dim).
  - Reserved SKUs: ui-reserved-32, ui-reserved-64, ui-reserved-128 with monthly commitment discounts (see table).
- Dedicated: monthly capacity-based pricing with three tiers (Standard, High-Memory, High-Throughput). Each tier includes a reserved baseline and a per-token overage rate.
- Private: licensing + support; custom pricing per customer.
Pricing table (example):
| SKU | Monthly price | Included throughput | Overage rate | Notes |
| ui-reserved-32 | $1,500 | 32 concurrent tokens/sec baseline | $0.00045/token | Good for small production teams |
| ui-reserved-64 | $2,800 | 64 concurrent tokens/sec baseline | $0.00040/token | Recommended for mid-tier |
| ui-reserved-128 | $5,200 | 128 concurrent tokens/sec baseline | $0.00036/token | Enterprise-grade |
Billing and migration notes:
- Customers on legacy reserved SKUs will be mapped to new SKUs one-month prior to GA and offered a migration credit for two billing cycles.
- Billing emits detailed cost_breakdown telemetry to allow customers to reconcile invoices.
Sales enablement:
- Updated pitch deck and pricing FAQ in sales-enablement/product-hub. Key objections and answers included in separate doc: product-pricing-faq-2027-10-15.json.
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference v21 — GA (2027-11-01)
Highlights:
- Introduced route-level cost controls and preferred_model_tier.
- Quantization presets (performance/balanced/compact) with console presets.
- New SKU-based reserved pricing for Hosted API.
- Console cost-simulator and per-route cost insights.
Fixed issues and improvements:
- Reduced median p99 latency by 8% for 256-token workloads (edge routing optimizations).
- Billing pipeline emits sku_id for all reserved allocations (fixes mismatch issue seen in beta).
Known issues:
- Some customers with extreme conversational prefix lengths (>4k tokens) may see KV-cache eviction causing higher latency; working on adaptive KV sizing (ETA M2).
Rollout notes:
- Week 0: Internal GA and dogfood (engineering + select internal teams).
- Week 1-2: Pilot customers (by invite) guided by Customer Success.
- Week 3-6: Gradual public rollout with feature-flag gate; default behavior remains legacy routing until explicit opt-in.
Telemetry & dashboards:
- New dashboards added under /dashboards/unified-inference/v21: cost-simulator, route-policy-usage, quant-profile-quality-regressions.
Post-release actions:
1) Run 30-day billing reconciliation job (Finance & Billing).
2) Collect pilot feedback and open follow-up tickets for UX improvements (Product).
3) Schedule ADRs for open design decisions within 2 weeks.
rollout_plan:
Canary and rollback plan:
1) Canary: enable route-level cost controls for 5% of EU traffic and 2 internal pilot customers. Watch p99 latency, cost per request, and model_quality_delta.
2) Validate: run 48-hour smoke tests and revenue/billing reconciliation for canary traffic.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks as metrics stay green.
Rollback procedure (step-by-step):
1) Flip feature-flag for affected routes in Control Plane UI.
2) Trigger automatic rollback script: /bin/rollback-route --route <id> --reason '<ticket>' (SRE on-call).
3) Verify downstream consumers and run end-to-end smoke tests.

SLOs and alert thresholds to monitor during rollout:

- Error rate: alert if 5xx > 0.5% for 10m window.
- Billing delta: alert if daily billing mismatch > 0.5% of expected daily revenue.
